notes: CDOT/Mayor's Press Office, Oct 9, 2015 release ('City of Chicago Surpasses Mayor Emanuel's Goal of Installing 100 Miles of Protected Bike Lanes, Commits to More'): 292-mile bikeway network (94mi bike lanes, 83.5mi buffered protected, 46mi off-street trails, 48.75mi marked shared lanes, 19.5mi barrier protected, 1.5mi neighborhood greenways).

CDOT/Mayor's Press Office, Sept 20, 2016 release ('...Named America's Top City for Cycling'): 292-mile bikeway network (245mi on-street bike lanes + 47mi off-street trails). A closer-dated April 2016 release separately cited 290 miles; essentially flat during 2016, this later/higher figure used.

CDOT, 'Complete Streets 2024 Highlights' official page: 'As of year-end 2024, Chicago's cycling network contains 478 miles of bike facilities' (installed over 15mi protected bike lanes and nearly 16mi neighborhood greenways during the year). Fits the established trend: 420mi (Mar 2023) to 478mi (end 2024) to 500mi (Sept 2025).
